subject: plastic cutting board microplastics
title: What If You Always Used a Plastic Cutting Board?

scenes.text: What if you chopped everything on a plastic cutting board? Switching boards isn't the easy fix.
Every knife strike carves a tiny groove, and the board sheds microscopic plastic specks into your food.
In a 2023 study, scientists chopped carrots and counted. One polyethylene board could shed fourteen to seventy-one million particles a year.
A polypropylene board came out around seventy-nine million a year, depending on how hard and how often you chop.
Then some good news: in lab tests, those polyethylene specks didn't noticeably affect the survival of mouse cells.
The twist? Wooden boards shed four to twenty-two times more particles than plastic ones. They're just made of wood.

description:
What if you always used a plastic cutting board? A 2023 study in Environmental Science & Technology estimated that chopping on polyethylene boards could release 14 to 71 million microplastic particles a year, and polypropylene boards about 79 million, depending on chopping style and force.
Polyethylene and wood microparticles had no substantial effect on mouse cell survival in lab tests, and wooden boards shed 4 to 22 times more microparticles than plastic ones.
